blocks.prompt: 2. Find the 8th term of the sequence, \(3, 3^{2}, 3^{3}, \ldots\)
blocks.explanation:
Is sequence ke terms 3 ki powers hain: \(3, 3^2, 3^3\). Har term pichle term ka 3 guna hai, yani yeh G.P. hai.
Diya kya hai? Pehle teen terms.
Find kya karna hai? 8th term \(a_8\).
Plan: \(a_1\) aur \(r\) pehchanein, phir \(a_8 = a_1 r^{7}\). Saath hi pattern se bhi jawab ki tasdeeq karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(3, 3^2, 3^3, \ldots\)
Humein find karna hai: \(a_8\).
Tareeqa: Pehle dikhayenge ke yeh G.P. hai (ratio barabar hai), phir formula \(a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}\) mein \(n = 8\) rakhenge. Yeh formula har G.P. ka koi bhi term seedha de deta hai.

\(a_1\) aur \(r\) nikalein
\[a_1 = 3\]
\[r = \dfrac{3^2}{3} = 3\]
Kyun: Ek hi base ki powers ko divide karein to powers minus hoti hain: \(3^2 \div 3^1 = 3^{2-1} = 3\). Agla ratio \(3^3 \div 3^2\) bhi 3 hai, is liye ratio har jagah barabar hai aur sequence pakka G.P. hai.

General term lagayein
\[a_8 = a_1 r^{7} = 3 \cdot 3^{7}\]
\[= 3^{8} = 6561\]
Kyun: 8th term ke liye power \(8 - 1 = 7\). Ek hi base ki powers multiply hon to powers jama hoti hain: \(3^1 \cdot 3^7 = 3^{8}\). Hisaab aasaan karne ke liye \(3^4 = 81\) aur \(3^8 = 81 \times 81 = 6561\).
Dhyan dein: \(3 \cdot 3^7\) ko \(9^7\) mat bana dijiye; base wohi 3 rehta hai, sirf powers jama hoti hain.

Tasdeeq: pattern se
\[a_n = 3^{n}\ \Rightarrow\ a_8 = 3^8\]
Kyun: Pehla term \(3^1\), doosra \(3^2\), teesra \(3^3\) hai, yani term ka number hi power hai. Is liye 8th term \(3^8\) hona chahiye, aur formula ne bhi yahi diya.
